source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
A single Chandler campus holds 169 MW of published IT capacity, 33 percent of Arizona's disclosed data center load and the largest disclosed campus in the state.

Arizona's disclosure is thin. Four facilities publish power figures, totaling 512 MW, while 57 facilities are mapped in the state. The 169 MW share is a share of what is disclosed, not of what exists, so the state's real footprint is larger and mostly unmeasured. CyrusOne's campus is the largest disclosed block by a wide margin, and that ranking rests on other operators not publishing.

For AI the binding number is power, not floor space. The campus pairs 169 MW with 2 million square feet of technical space, about 85 watts per square foot. The same capacity supports roughly 4,200 racks at 40 kW each, a training-class density, or roughly 16,900 racks at 10 kW, an inference-class density. The published record does not say which the campus is built for, and that choice determines how much compute the 169 MW actually buys.

The certifications, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, ISO 27001, TIA-942 and Green Globes, show the campus is qualified to host regulated financial, healthcare and federal work. They do not show that any such tenant is present. The record carries no street address or coordinates, no tenant names, no measure of how much of the 169 MW is drawn, and no power source or interconnection detail. The suitability score of 83 lists announced expansion as a missing input, so nothing here indicates whether the campus grows.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
